narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 21 % chance you won’t pass your final year, which is above the 10 % threshold the school uses to require extra help. That’s why you’re being asked to take remedial courses now—so you can strengthen the areas that are making success harder to reach.

The single biggest factor working in your favor is that you’ve never failed a class before. Students with a clean record tend to do better, and that history is giving the model confidence you can still turn things around. However, two other factors are pulling the prediction the other way. First, your mother’s education level is lower than most of your classmates’ mothers, and the model sees this as a small but noticeable risk. Second, your guardian is your father rather than your mother, which the model also treats as a slight disadvantage compared to the typical student.

None of these things mean you’re destined to fail, but together they suggest you’ll benefit from a bit more structured support. The remedial courses are designed to give you that extra practice and attention, especially in the subjects where you might be struggling. You can also talk with your teachers about study strategies or ask your family for help at home—even small changes in routine can make a difference. The goal isn’t just to pass this year, but to build habits that will keep you on track for the future.
